newsitem.title: IRAQ: Baghdad explosions injure five, says group.
newsitem.headline: Baghdad explosions injure five, says group.

text.p: An Iraq-based Iranian opposition group said two explosions rocked the Iraqi capital Baghdad on Tuesday, injuring five people, after mortar shells were aimed at its headquarters.

A spokesman for the Mujahideen Khalq group blamed what he called "the Mullah terrorists ruling Iran" for the attack. The group has military bases close to the border with Iran and has vowed to topple Tehran's clerical regime.
He said the explosions wrecked a hospital laboratory and another building.

"At least five people have been injured and one of them had his leg amputated and Baghdad's central laboratory has been wrecked and another hospital partly damaged," the spokesman told Reuters. There was no immediate word from Iraqi authorities.

He said the explosions, which were heard in many parts of the Iraqi capital, resulted from the firing of shells from what he described as "super mortar guns" originally directed at the Mujahideen headquarters in Baghdad.
He said one of the mortar shells created a crater five metres (15 feet) in diameter and three metres (10 feet) deep. He said it fell 500 metres away from the group's office.
"Three such mortars were fired against our headquarters from a distance of 600 metres but only two of them exploded," he said.

He said the ceiling of the central laboratory in Baghdad had collapsed and the al-Haydari hospital was partly damaged. Heavy damage was also inflicted on the building of the Iraqi Writers Union which was hit by one of the shells, he added.
He said the attackers had timed their mortar guns and hidden them in a lorry about 700 metres away from the Mujahideen office in the heart of the Iraqi capital.
The explosion had smashed windows in the Mujahideen building in Baghdad but inflicted no injuries "on our combatants and all the wounded were Iraqi civilians".
"The number of the wounded could be much more than five and they are being treated at Ibn Nafis hospital in Baghdad, he said. "We are told some are in critical condition."
The group says Iran has mounted 43 attacks against its headquarters and personnel in the area of Baghdad since 1993, killing at least 10 and injuring many others.

Iraq and Iran have accused each other of sheltering opposition groups. Baghdad has formally blamed Iran for the December 12 attempt on the life of the son of Iraqi leader Saddam Hussein. Iran has denied any involvement.

Tehran has accused Iraq of allowing the Mujahideen to cross the border for possible attacks on targets inside Iran. The Iranian news agency said this week that Iranian tribesmen and government forces killed five members of an Iraq-based opposition group in clashes in western Iran.
